task.title: Report an edit dropped because its comment was removed elsewhere
task.description:
When one person edits a comment while another removes it on a different clone, the removal stands and the edit is dropped. That outcome is deliberate. What is wrong is how the person who made the edit finds out: their `workbook sync` prints `reconciled replayed 0 local operation(s); 1 already applied upstream`, which reads as if the edit went through. The edited text survives only in that clone's local `refs/workbook/reconciled/<id>/` refs, which are capped at three per task and never pushed.

Found on 2026-11-21 by the review of "Let only a comment's author edit it" (PR #213). The behavior is the same on a build without that change, so it was not fixed there. It runs against the concurrency rule that prefers showing a conflict over silently discarding someone's intent.

## What is needed

- Sync output, text and JSON, says that an edit was dropped because its comment had been removed, names the task and the comment, and says where the dropped text can be recovered from.
- The background sync reports the same thing through whatever it already uses to tell a person about a conflict nobody was present for.
- A decision on whether the dropped text should be kept somewhere more durable than a capped local ref.

## Done when

- A person whose edit lost to a removal is told so by the command that discovers it, and by the next command after a background sync discovers it.
- A test covers both delivery orders on two clones.
- `docs/reference.md` describes the report.
